haiku-low.q1: At enqueue, when the caller's transaction inserts the pending row; if that transaction rolls back, no row exists and nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers the message after 30 seconds, possibly to another consumer.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts, waiting 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes between them; then marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update, then order_confirmed (each 3+ days), then password_reset. password_reset moves only after order_confirmed shows p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 s.
haiku-low.q5: The notification's id (UUID from row insert) as idempotency_key. MailRelay drops a repeat with that key within 24 hours, returning success.
haiku-low.q6: A relay publishes the row to the broker; the service consumes it. The monolith is done once the broker confirms, marking the row handed_off.
haiku-low.q7: The enqueue_notification call decides, reading flag notify.route.<type> when inserting the row; it sets route to service or monolith, once and permanently.
haiku-low.q8: The service's deliveries insert, keyed by the notification id: a repeat finds the id and inserts nothing. MailRelay drops repeats with the same key.
haiku-low.q9: After committing the deliveries insert, before any send. If it crashes before acking, redelivery finds the id; no second send.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's deliveries table. The service's sender acts on it, skipping rows until due and marking them failed after 5 attempts.
haiku-low.q11: They stay with the service, which finishes them. Rows already marked service are not moved; only new notifications route to the monolith.
haiku-low.q12: Per notification: id, type, email, payload and created_at. Email content is rendered in the Notification Service, where templates now live.

sonnet.q1: It becomes durable when enqueue_notification inserts a pending row into the monolith's notifications table inside the caller's transaction. Whether the caller's transaction commits or rolls back decides it: on rollback the row never exists and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The broker redelivers it, possibly to another consumer, if it is not acknowledged within 30 s (at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: Up to 5 attempts. After attempts 1 to 4 fail, the next attempt is 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes later. After the 5th failure the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: One type at a time, each chosen by its flag: shipping_update first (run at least 3 days), then order_confirmed (at least 3 days), then password_reset last. Before password_reset moves, the service must have shown p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 s on order_confirmed.
sonnet.q5: The idempotency_key, which is the notification's id (a UUID made when the row is inserted). If MailRelay accepted a send with the same key in the last 24 hours, it drops the repeat and returns success.
sonnet.q6: A relay loop on each monolith instance takes pending route=service rows with the row lock, publishes one message per row to the broker topic notifications.requested, and the service consumes them. The monolith is done with a row when the broker confirms it stored the message, and the row is set to handed_off. It never learns the send outcome.
sonnet.q7: enqueue_notification decides, inside the caller's transaction at insert time. It reads the flag notify.route.<type> and sets the row's route to service if the flag is on, otherwise monolith. The route is never changed afterward.
sonnet.q8: The deliveries insert is keyed by id, so if the id already exists nothing is inserted and no second send is created. The MailRelay idempotency key (the id) also makes MailRelay drop a repeated send.
sonnet.q9: It acknowledges only after the local deliveries insert has committed, and before the send, which happens later in the sender loop. If it crashes before acknowledging, the broker redelivers and the insert finds the row already there or creates it.
sonnet.q10: In the service's own database, in the deliveries row (status, attempt count, next attempt time). The service sender loop acts on it, taking due pending rows with the row lock.
sonnet.q11: Nothing changes for them. Rows already marked route=service stay with the service, which finishes them. Only new notifications get route=monolith. If the service is broken, those rows wait until it recovers, which is flagged as an open question.
sonnet.q12: A message with id, type, email, payload and created_at (the enqueue time). The email content is rendered in the Notification Service, from the template, by the sender.
